source.title: SAE-V: Interpreting Multimodal Models for Enhanced Alignment
source.authors: Hantao Lou; Chang-Ye Li; Jia-Ming Ji; Yao-Dong Yang

record.tranche_reason: Applies sparse autoencoders to multimodal LLMs, a new model setting, and reports feature-interpretability and reconstruction results. It does not test toy-model superposition geometry.
record.gate_note: The paper reports SAE feature examples, activation sparsity (L0), reconstruction comparisons, and transfer results that bear on V4. Alignment-data filtering results and image-patch classification results are omitted because they measure the paper's filtering methods' performance, not feature recovery or superposition. It cites Toy Models of Superposition but does not reproduce or test its results.
record.test_reason: This is a methods paper. It uses SAEs (premised on superposition) as a tool and reports how its SAE-V performs against a standard SAE on L0, reconstruction loss, transfer, patch filtering and alignment data filtering. Its only feature-level evidence is two hand-picked examples (Fig. 3) showing the tool works. It does not measure whether LLM features are spread across neurons, or how completely and faithfully a dictionary recovers them. No version is tested; the reader's T3/V4 'tests' call is overturned.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that SAE-V extracts interpretable features from MLLMs and transfers to their base LLMs. They report SAE-V reconstruction loss at 38.3% and 50.6% of SAE's on MLLMs and LLMs. They also conclude that SAE-V-based data filtering reaches more than 110% of full-data alignment performance with less than 50% of the data. They make no claim about superposition itself.
record.recipe_differences: Uses sparse-autoencoder training and multimodal feature interpretation, not the toy-network feature competition and geometry experiments of Toy Models of Superposition.
record.method_sensitivity: Results depend on model architecture and whether the SAE was trained on multimodal or text-only data; L0 patterns differ among models.

fits_no_version.finding: An SAE-V trained on multimodal data gives interpretable cross-modal features in LLaVA-NeXT-7B (Doberman, symmetry). A text-trained SAE reconstructs worse than zero ablation on Chameleon-7B and Anole-7B.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE dictionaries recover cross-modal interpretable features in MLLMs only when trained on multimodal activations.

record.code_released: GitHub and Hugging Face are stated as release locations; URLs not stated
record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 267, 2025
record.problems: The paper offers only qualitative examples for interpretability and no ground-truth feature-recovery metric. Reconstruction results are presented in figures without tabulated values; the authors note that the theory behind the feature similarity and model performance relationship is not fully revealed and evaluate only text and vision modalities.
record.rows_left_out: Alignment data-filtering performance, image-patch filtering, and ImageNet/VQA outcomes were not included because they do not measure the versions' feature-recovery or superposition claims.

untested.parts: No toy models, sparsity sweep, phase transition or geometry.
No capacity or importance analysis of neuron polysemanticity.
No alternative causes of polysemanticity examined.

No measure of features distributed across neurons. No quantitative assessment of how well, or how faithfully, the SAE recovers features: only two illustrative examples plus method-comparison L0 and reconstruction.
No test of completeness, stability across seeds or sizes, or canonicality. The appendix notes only about 30k of 65k–131k features activate, but this is not analysed.
No comparison of 1-D and multi-dimensional features.

record.verdict_notes: This is an SAE application and methods paper. Toy Models of Superposition is cited only in related work. Every quantitative result is SAE-V versus SAE, or filtering performance. Reconstruction values are given only in figures. If the corpus treats SAE interpretability demonstrations in new model families as V4 evidence, r1 and r2 could be relinked to V4 as weak, qualitative, cherry-picked support. They should not count as a test.

versions.untested_parts: No toy networks, feature-over-dimension sweep, sparsity-dependent transition, or geometry test.
No test of capacity pressure, neuron polysemanticity, or allocation of dedicated versus shared dimensions.
No test of alternative causes of polysemantic neurons or whether polysemanticity indicates superposition.
Does not directly measure feature distribution across neurons or compare recovered SAE features with ground-truth features; evidence is qualitative examples and reconstruction-based.
Transfer and example features are reported, but completeness, stability, and canonical status are not tested.
No comparison of one-dimensional directions with multidimensional features.

rows.subject: LLaVA-NeXT-7B
rows.operation_detail: Qualitative example of SAE-V feature #44031 activating across text and image examples for Doberman dogs.
rows.measure: Cross-modal semantic consistency / interpretability of feature examples
rows.value: The authors describe strong activation for Doberman dogs across both modalities.
rows.note: Qualitative example; no quantitative feature-recovery measure.
rows.check: A single cherry-picked feature example illustrating SAE-V. No measure of feature recovery, frequency or distribution across neurons, so it cannot bear on V4.

rows.subject: LLaVA-NeXT-7B
rows.operation_detail: Qualitative example of SAE-V feature #11105 activating on symmetry-related text and image patterns.
rows.measure: Cross-modal semantic consistency / interpretability of feature examples
rows.value: The authors describe the feature as capturing symmetry across modalities, with image activation aligned to symmetry patterns.
rows.note: Qualitative example; no quantitative feature-recovery measure.
rows.check: A single cherry-picked feature example illustrating SAE-V. It is not a measurement of how features are represented in the model.

rows.subject: Chameleon-7B
rows.operation_detail: Compared SAE-V and SAE mean activated-feature count (L0).
rows.note: The lower activation count indicates greater activation sparsity, but L0 alone does not establish recovery of interpretable features.
rows.check: Compares the study's own method (SAE-V) with SAE on L0, which is method performance. The SAE baseline of 24757.6 is called a text-trained SAE failure on unseen vision tokens.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: SAE-V feature examples and reconstruction results in the tested multimodal models
reader_labels.reason: The authors give cross-modal interpretable feature examples and report SAE-V reconstruction superior to SAE across tested models (r1-r2, r8-r15).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: SAE trained on text data and applied to multimodal models
reader_labels.reason: Reconstruction varies by model, and the paper reports SAE performing worse than zero activation on Chameleon-7B and Anole-7B; this indicates results depend on training data and model setting (r11-r12).
